models_evaluated: Lung cancer 2-year mortality model (mean heart dose and gross tumor volume)

links.outcome: Calibration and discrimination of lung cancer model when applied to esophageal cancer patients
links.effect: dCRT needed intercept adjustment (c-statistic 0.67, 95%CI 0.58 to 0.75); nCRT initial miscalibration (CS 1.72) required intercept and slope recalibration (c-statistic 0.62, 95%CI 0.57 to 0.67).
links.quote: For nCRT patients the model needed adjustment of both the slope and the intercept because of initial miscalibration in the validation population (CITL 0.00; CS 1.72).

models_evaluated: Lung cancer-based 2-year total mortality prediction model using mean heart dose and gross tumor volume

links.effect: nCRT patients had initial miscalibration requiring slope and intercept adjustment; CITL 0.00, CS 1.72.
links.quote: For nCRT patients the model needed adjustment of both the slope and the intercept because of initial miscalibration in the validation population (CITL 0.00; CS 1.72).

links.effect: After recalibration, calibration was CITL 0 and CS 1 in nCRT patients.
links.quote: After recalibration, the model showed perfect calibration (i.e., CITL 0, CS 1), as is common after recalibration.

links.outcome: model calibration in new target population
links.effect: initial miscalibration in neo-adjuvant chemoradiotherapy patients with calibration-in-the-large 0.00 and calibration slope 1.72
links.quote: For nCRT patients the model needed adjustment of both the slope and the intercept because of initial miscalibration in the validation population (CITL 0.00; CS 1.72).
